studies.label: Writer experiment: short-story writing with optional GPT-4 story ideas, rated by separate evaluators
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individual writers were randomized; there are no treatment-assignment clusters. Writer-story similarity outcomes use robust standard errors with one story per writer (PDF p. 8, Statistical analysis).

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Write without any mention of or access to generative AI. Writers admitting outside AI use were excluded. The analyzed arm count is printed in Supplement sciadv.adn5290_sm.pdf, p. 5, Table S1, Observations row.

arms.name: Human with one GenAI idea
arms.description: Optional request for one three-sentence GPT-4 story idea from a fixed prompt; the writer then writes the story and cannot copy and paste the idea. Analyzed count is printed in PDF p. 2, Results: Of the 100 writers in the Human with one GenAI idea condition.

arms.name: Human with five GenAI ideas
arms.description: Optional requests for up to five three-sentence GPT-4 story ideas from fixed prompts; all requested ideas remain visible and cannot be copied and pasted. Analyzed count is printed in PDF p. 2, Results: 93 of 98 writers in this condition requested an idea.

studies.task: Write an English story of exactly eight sentences on a randomly assigned adventure topic (open seas, jungle, or another planet) for a teenage and young adult audience.

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-4 via OpenAI's GPT API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Materials and Methods, Writer study and experimental conditions, GPT API and fixed story-idea prompt; the model release year and dated snapshot are not printed

preregistration.where: AsPredicted.org, ID 136723 (main PDF p. 8); complete copy in Supplement sciadv.adn5290_sm.pdf, pp. 76-77, Section 9. The preregistration page was read from the rendered PDF because its text layer is garbled.
preregistration.primary_outcome: Evaluator-rated novelty and usefulness indices. Section 9, questions 3 and 5, specifies OLS by assigned condition and a combined-AI main analysis conditional on no significant difference between the AI conditions. Individual components and alternative econometric specifications are preregistered robustness tests; emotional outcomes are exploratory; neither similarity outcome is listed.

estimates.notes: The analysis is at the rating level. The paper specifies robust SEs clustered by evaluator, not by the randomized writer (PDF p. 8). se_basis is coded rating to flag that the uncertainty does not account for repeated ratings of each writer; regression.se_type, when present, is clustered_cluster for evaluator clusters. n_units is the printed total of evaluations across the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement prints regression SEs and Human-only intercept estimates with their SEs. Neither document prints rating-level or participant-level SDs for this outcome or numerical confidence-interval endpoints. The reported b is an unstandardized coefficient. The percentage is transcribed in its printed units; no effect or arm mean is derived. The rating code is used because the schema has no evaluator category; it does not assert that the paper treated every rating as independent. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. Supplement Table S3 confirms the significant one-idea result printed on main PDF p. 3; the wording on main PDF p. 2 emphasizing statistically significant gains only in the five-idea arm remains inconsistent.

estimates.notes: Each writer contributes one story; the paper specifies OLS with robust SEs for writer-study outcomes (PDF p. 8), so se_basis is participant. n_units is the printed total of stories in the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement supplies the robust regression SE and the Human-only intercept SE; numerical confidence-interval endpoints and AI-arm SDs are not printed. The printed Human-only intercept supplies the control mean; AI-arm means are not printed. The coefficient and p-value are transcribed in the cosine-similarity-times-100 scale; higher means less diversity. sources.quote: We will run robustness tests for each of these, which will include different econometric specifications and variants (e.g., sub-items, discretization) of the outcome measures.

estimates.notes: The analysis is at the rating level. The paper specifies robust SEs clustered by evaluator, not by the randomized writer (PDF p. 8). se_basis is coded rating to flag that the uncertainty does not account for repeated ratings of each writer; regression.se_type, when present, is clustered_cluster for evaluator clusters. n_units is the printed total of evaluations across the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement prints regression SEs and Human-only intercept estimates with their SEs. Neither document prints rating-level or participant-level SDs for this outcome or numerical confidence-interval endpoints. Supplement Table S3 supplies the component coefficient and SE. The component analyses were preregistered as robustness tests, not primary tests (Supplement Section 9, question 5). Item wording is available in Supplement Section 1 and the evaluator screenshots in Section 8. No number is estimated from a figure. The rating code is used because the schema has no evaluator category; it does not assert that the paper treated every rating as independent. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast.

sources.quote: We will run OLS regressions predicting novelty and usefulness by condition, and run these regressions for both creators and evaluators.

estimates.notes: Each writer contributes one story; the paper specifies OLS with robust SEs for writer-study outcomes (PDF p. 8), so se_basis is participant. n_units is the printed total of stories in the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement supplies the robust regression SE and the Human-only intercept SE; numerical confidence-interval endpoints and AI-arm SDs are not printed. This outcome concerns resemblance to an AI idea, not diversity across different people, and is coded with_ai/other. The screening form moved former outcome S1-O10 into its notes solely because of its outcome cap; the extraction specification has no such cap, so both contrasts are retained with form_outcome_id null. Supplement Section 3 specifies randomly sampling an AI idea generated for the same story topic, corroborating main PDF p. 5 and clarifying the conflicting same-condition wording on main PDF p. 8. Treatment means are not derived by adding coefficients to the printed control mean. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. The Human-only SD comes from the full Human group in Table S12; statistics for the self-selected AI-use groups are not substituted for randomized AI arms. Table S11 prints the coefficient as 4.288, while the main text prints 4.29; the main-text value is retained, with the supplement precision documented here. Neither similarity outcome is listed in the complete preregistration, so preregistered_primary is no.

estimates.notes: Each writer contributes one story; the paper specifies OLS with robust SEs for writer-study outcomes (PDF p. 8), so se_basis is participant. n_units is the printed total of stories in the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement supplies the robust regression SE and the Human-only intercept SE; numerical confidence-interval endpoints and AI-arm SDs are not printed. This outcome concerns resemblance to an AI idea, not diversity across different people, and is coded with_ai/other. The screening form moved former outcome S1-O10 into its notes solely because of its outcome cap; the extraction specification has no such cap, so both contrasts are retained with form_outcome_id null. Supplement Section 3 specifies randomly sampling an AI idea generated for the same story topic, corroborating main PDF p. 5 and clarifying the conflicting same-condition wording on main PDF p. 8. Treatment means are not derived by adding coefficients to the printed control mean. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. The Human-only SD comes from the full Human group in Table S12; statistics for the self-selected AI-use groups are not substituted for randomized AI arms. Table S11 prints the coefficient as 4.105, while the main text prints 4.11; the main-text value is retained, with the supplement precision documented here. Neither similarity outcome is listed in the complete preregistration, so preregistered_primary is no.

open_items: The total randomized count and randomized counts by arm are not printed. The number who began the study is not a randomized count. The paper excludes non-completers and Human-only writers who admitted AI use; the timing and arm allocation of all dropouts are not provided (PDF p. 7).

The supplement prints unadjusted Human-only means as regression constants and numerical regression SEs, but not the AI-arm means (apart from the main-text one-idea usefulness mean), AI-arm SDs, or numerical confidence-interval endpoints. Creativity ratings and across-people similarity still lack outcome SDs; only the Human-only story-to-AI-idea similarity SD is printed in Table S12. Both AI-arm levels of the across-people outcome remain unavailable. No values are calculated from constants, coefficients, plots or p-values.

Evaluator-rated results cluster SEs by evaluator rather than writer, including the fixed-effect robustness models in Supplement Table S4. se_basis remains rating. A writer-level analysis or uncertainty accounting for repeated ratings of each randomized writer is still needed for pooling under codebook section 10.
Neither the main text nor the supplement states the GPT-4 release year, a dated model snapshot, or the OpenAI embedding model. ai_tool.year remains null.

Main PDF p. 2 describes statistically significant index gains as coming from the five-idea arm, while p. 3 reports significant one-idea results. Supplement Table S3 confirms the one-idea coefficients and their significance markers but does not explain the main-text wording. Main-text numbers are preserved.

The preregistration in Supplement Section 9 makes the combined-AI main analysis conditional on no significant difference between the AI conditions. The paper reports the combined contrast despite the significant five-versus-one usefulness comparison in the main text; no explanation of this departure is printed.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-09 by checking both raw extractions against the complete markdown conversion, read in consecutive chunks through the references and publisher information page, and text extracted from every page of the saved PDF with PyMuPDF. Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 were also inspected directly in memory; no figure values were digitized and no other file was written. The supplied diff has no estimates unique to either extractor. All eligible outcome/contrast entries in the screening form are represented, and the self-assessments are listed in not_extracted. Both extractors already retained the story-to-AI-idea anchoring contrasts omitted under the screening outcome cap; those remain with form_outcome_id null. No estimates were added. Agreed counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person were independently checked. There is one between-person writer RCT with optional AI-idea access, not a within-person study; the evaluators are a separate sample. AI was available during production in the AI arms, and there is no after-AI outcome. The only across_people outcome compares each story with the average embedding of other writers in its condition; anchoring to an AI idea is with_ai/other. Each writer supplies one story. Counts of writers and ratings remain separate: n_units is the printed full analysis count, not a two-arm subtotal, and n_total is null for two-arm contrasts whose participant total is not printed. The combined-AI comparisons cover all analyzed writers and use the printed study total. All unavailable counts, means, SDs, SEs, interval endpoints, and figure-only effects remain null; no study statistics were calculated. Printed percentages are paper_effect type other in percent units, not standardized effects. Quotes copy PDF text with whitespace collapsed and preserve printed signs and precision, including the coefficient printed as −0.200. Sources retain discretionary and line-break hyphens. The resolution list also records evaluator-clustering differences omitted by the supplied diff. The novelty and usefulness indices are identified as preregistered; the five-versus-one test has an uncertain preregistration status, as stated in its notes. AI take-up is optional and the paper describes intention-to-treat comparisons of assigned conditions, but assigned writers were also excluded for noncompletion or admitted outside AI use. Shared controls and the combined-AI records reuse participants; the screening form identifies no other paper sharing this sample. Separate supplementary materials are not available in the saved document. Supplement update: The preceding paragraph documents the earlier main-PDF-only reconciliation. The complete supplied supplement conversion and PDF have now been reviewed, including the survey screenshots and the rendered preregistration; their text-layer limitations were checked directly. All original numerical values and historical review logs are preserved. The source and estimate notes now identify the supplementary additions. Table S1 supplies analyzed writer counts; Tables S3, S6, S11 and S13 supply coefficients, SEs and unadjusted Human-only intercept estimates; Table S12 supplies the full Human-only anchoring SD. All combined component contrasts and full-sample Table S4 assigned-condition robustness coefficients are included. Covariate-adjusted constants are not recorded as arm means; omnibus multi-regressor F tests are not recorded as individual-arm tests. No outcome means, SDs, test statistics, intervals or effect sizes were calculated. Earlier uncertainty about primary status is resolved from the full preregistration, with the conditional pooling plan documented. Similarity outcomes are not listed there. Remaining gaps and the unresolved reporting inconsistencies are retained in open_items.

supplement_changes.new: The analysis is at the rating level. The paper specifies robust SEs clustered by evaluator, not by the randomized writer (PDF p. 8). se_basis is coded rating to flag that the uncertainty does not account for repeated ratings of each writer; regression.se_type, when present, is clustered_cluster for evaluator clusters. n_units is the printed total of evaluations across the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement prints regression SEs and Human-only intercept estimates with their SEs. Neither document prints rating-level or participant-level SDs for this outcome or numerical confidence-interval endpoints. The reported b is an unstandardized coefficient. The percentage is transcribed in its printed units; no effect or arm mean is derived. The rating code is used because the schema has no evaluator category; it does not assert that the paper treated every rating as independent. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. Supplement Table S3 confirms the significant one-idea result printed on main PDF p. 3; the wording on main PDF p. 2 emphasizing statistically significant gains only in the five-idea arm remains inconsistent.

supplement_kept.why_the_flag_is_wrong: Confirmed by direct inspection of the rendered supplement PDF p. 77 (zero-based page index 76). The quoted passage is printed verbatim, with line breaks collapsed. PyMuPDF get_text() returns misencoded glyphs and control characters on this page, and the markdown conversion inherits the corrupted text. The failed literal match is therefore a PDF text-layer error, not an incorrect quotation or locator. Question 5 explicitly describes sub-items and alternative econometric specifications as robustness tests. This supports the existing preregistered_primary=no value for this component or robustness estimate.
